title: Rewrite request coalescer and prefetch sharding to reduce lock contention
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Background: Over the last year we've observed increased tail latency and CPU churn on multi-tenant inference nodes under mixed workloads. Root cause analysis points at a hot-path contention inside the request coalescer (legacy mutex-based merge) and the monolithic KV prefetcher which serializes shard scans during heavy cold-starts. These problems amplify when request size variance increases and when short-lived interactive workloads compete with long-running batched jobs.

Problem statement: The current coalescer holds global locks for request merging and for coordinating prefetch across all slots. This leads to contention spikes that: (1) increase p95/p99 latencies under moderate QPS, (2) prevent effective slot reclamation during GC, and (3) blow up CPU scheduling for small requests.

Goals:
- Remove global contention in the request coalescer by moving to a lock-free per-lane coalescing ring and a light-weight epoch-based coordinator.
- Repartition KV prefetch into shard-aware workers (prefetch shards) to avoid global scans and to allow incremental prefetch backpressure per shard.
- Keep behavior backwards-compatible: feature-flag the new coalescer and shard prefetcher for gradual rollout.
- Measurable targets: p95 inference latency reduced by 10–20% for interactive workloads in canary, overall CPU utilization on inference nodes reduced by 12% under mixed traffic.

Technical approach:
1) Coalescer rewrite: introduce a coalescer lane per worker thread using a lock-free SPSC ring buffer for joining small requests that target the same model/token-window. Use an epoch counter for safe reclamation when lanes are resized or drained. Central coordinator only handles lane-to-resource mapping and rare reconfiguration events.
2) Prefetch sharding: break the monolithic prefetch queue into N prefetch shards keyed by KV shard id. Each shard has its own bounded worker pool and local priority queue for prefix warmups. Implement backpressure tokens so that long-running prefetches do not starve short critical warms.
3) Lease reclamation: adjust slot reclamation to query prefetch shard state instead of global prefetch counters to avoid false positive reclamation during heavy prefetch storms.
4) Migration & flags: add runtime flags: runtime.coalescer_v2_enabled, runtime.prefetch_shard_count (default 0 for off). Prepare convenience toggles in the console for canary control.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests cover lane resizing, epoch reclamation, and shard failover scenarios.
- Canary run with 3 dedicated hosts shows p95 latency improvement >=10% for short 1–64 token requests and no regression for long requests.
- No memory leaks across repeated lane reconfiguration cycles (stress test 1M requests).
- Rollout flag can be switched off and nodes return to previous state without lost in-flight requests.

Monitoring / Observability:
- Add coalescer metrics: lanes_total, lane_contention_count, lane_merge_ratio, epoch_reclaims.
- Prefetch shard metrics: shard_queue_depth, shard_prefetch_duration_histogram, shard_backpressure_events.
- Create dashboard tile in Console runtime-1.22 -> Performance to compare pre/post canary.

Rollout plan:
- Merge behind feature flags. Run canary on small fleet (canary-rt-3).
- 72h canary with synthetic and production shadow traffic. If alarms: revert flag.
- Staged rollout by region and node class.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Complexity: lock-free lanes increase implementation complexity and increase risk of GC/ABA bugs; mitigated by epoch reclamation and thorough unit testing.
- Prefetch shard count tuning: too many shards may increase overhead; default off and gradual ramp.
- Interaction with existing batcher: ensure compatibility with continuous batching contract and commit semantics.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/REQ-62834 (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 (WIP)
- Bench harness: https://go.redwood/perf/bench/req-coalescer-2026

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the runtime hot-path rewrite and prefetch partitioning. Follow-up tickets will address fine-grained scheduling policies and autoscaler hints once the contention sources are eliminated.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Miguel Santos: Created ticket after correlating node CPU spikes with coalescer metrics during the Feb outage. Attached flamegraphs and initial hypothesis.

2026-02-14 - Aisha Khan: Spiked a prototype lane-based coalescer locally. Early results: merge ratio improved 2.3x, but saw an ABA issue when lane resized under GC. Added epoch-based reclamation plan.

2026-02-18 - Priya Raman (SRE): Please ensure we add metrics for shard_backpressure_events and include alert thresholds: >100 events / 5m triggers investigation. Also requested trace ids to link prefetch events to customer traces.
2026-02-21 - Miguel Santos: Integrated prefetch shards with bounded workers. Stress run (100k requests/s simulated) showed 18% lower CPU and p95 down by ~12ms for 1–64 token requests in dev-cluster.

2026-02-25 - Code Review - Ben Carter: Review feedback - prefer explicit memory fences in ring buffer implementation and add a deterministic unit test for lane draining ordering. Assigned follow-up to ENG-62835 (internal helper tests).

2026-03-01 - QA - Lina Patel: Running extended canary on canary-rt-3 with production shadow traffic. After 24h saw stable improvements; two minor regressions observed on edge case where prefetch shard worker crashed under OOM; added heap guard and restart policy.

2026-03-04 - Aisha Khan: Pulled request coalescer PR into runtime/integration branch. Integration tests green except for intermittent telemetry delay (investigating). Prepared rollback playbook and console toggle for rapid disable.
2026-03-05 - Miguel Santos: Updated acceptance criteria to include 1M stress test. Scheduling follow-up retro after rollout. Next steps: finalize PR, prepare release notes for runtime-1.22.
